To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The nano-crystallites of the soft magnetic Fe-Zr-N films are magnetically correlated and the magnetic properties of the films can be studied by Lorentz TEM and electron holography.”
the nano-crystallization in Fe-Zr-N alloys is accompanied by the formation of an ultra-soft magnetic phase, which is characterized by a large magnetization fluctuation.
the nano-crystallite size and the magnetic domain size are the same and that the magnetic domains are in a state of a rapid fluctuation of their magnetization vector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the magnetization structure of thin magnetic films.
the study of the magnetic structure and magnetic properties of soft ferromagnetic films by LTEM and electron holography.
the investigation of soft magnetic materials by means of electron holography, LTEM and magnetic force microscopy (MFM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic properties of nano-crystallized films are determined not only by the grain size, but also by the fluctuating amplitude of the magnetization.
the magnetization vector is not a constant vector but fluctuates in both magnitude and direction.

nano-crystallization of the soft magnetic films leads to a significant decrease of the magnetic permeability and to an increase of the coercive field, which can be explained by the formation of a new phase with a higher magnetic anisotropy and a higher saturation magnetization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel analysis of the LTEM image of nano-crystallized films and we have shown that not only the direction of the magnetic vector makes a small-angle wiggled correlated motion, but also the magnetization modulus has a rapid fluctuation.
the nano-crystallite films exhibit a strong fluctuation of the transversely magnetized nano-crystallites.
the LTEM technique is able to detect the magnetic fluctuations in nano-crystallyne soft magnetic films.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a new type of LTEM imaging technique can be used to study the magnetic softness of nano-crystallized films.
the amplitude of the magnetization fluctuation in nano-crystALLine films is comparable with the amplitude of magnetization in the bulk material.
the amplitude of the transverse magnetization is much higher than the longitudinal magnetization.
